transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-11 14:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rios (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood CSM), Jenna Patel (Solara Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Solara Security), Dr. Priya Menon (Solara CTO), Evan Morris (Eng Lead)

Summary / Topics (auto): MSA/DPA redline review; SLA and latency expectations for clinical inference; pricing approval timeline and pilot/onboarding plan.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll give a quick 2 minute agenda — legal redlines, security Qs, sla and pricing timeline, and then next steps. Jenna, want to confirm procurement goals?
[00:28] Jenna (Solara Procurement): Yeah thanks Maya. We're trying to finalize vendor contracting this quarter — so ideally PO in the next two weeks, that's kind of our target. We did a quick pass on the MSA and have a few redlines, esp around liability and data processing.
[00:45] Maya: Great, that's the timeline we'd hoped for. We'll prioritize the MSA redline. Carlos, i'll hand the technical and security parts to you.
[01:02] Carlos (Redwood SE): Cool, hi all. Quick note — for the latency thing, we've got two options: hosted api for fast time-to-value, or dedicated capacity if you need consistent p99s. For clinical inference i'd recommend Dedicated or Private depending on residency.
[01:28] Liam (Solara Security): Quick question — is Redwood Private available as VPC only or can it be on-prem? We have some regulated datasets that need strict controls; also KMS/HSM integration is a must.
[01:46] Carlos: Yes, Private supports VPC deployments and we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. KMS integration is supported — we can do customer-managed keys, HSM via our KMS provider plugins. I'll share the integration doc.
[02:08] Dr. Priya (CTO): When you say Dedicated, are we talking reserved GPU pools? Our main worry is p99 latency under bursty load for real-time triage features.
[02:24] Carlos: Exactly, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies. For the triage use-case, we suggest a mix of small q models plus quantization; we typically hit <200ms p99 with the config i'll send but it depends on seq length and concurrency.
[02:44] Evan (Eng Lead): Is that measured with prefix caching? We have a lot of repeated prompts for chart summarization.
[02:58] Carlos: Yes, prefix and KV cache reduce token cost and latency. Quick caveat: caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes; cold-starts still see higher latency.
[03:15] Jenna: On the MSA page 6, there's an indemnity clause that legal wants broadened. Is Redwood flexible on liability caps for healthcare customers?
[03:29] Maya: We can take a look, we do have enterprise terms we can offer, but it depends on deal size and risk profile. We'll surface the options in the redline.
[03:44] Liam: Also DPA — we need HIPAA-specific language and data residency in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Can you commit to data residency and audit logs?
[03:59] Asha (CSM): We log all request/response metadata for auditing, and retention controls are configurable. For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated to reduce surface area. I'll include our audit log retention options in the packet.
[04:18] Carlos: small note — sometimes the transcript of our product name shows up as 'Reedwood' in docs, so legal may see inconsistent refs, but we'll make sure all names are consistent in the package.
[04:33] Dr. Priya: Good to call out — we also need SOC2 and ISO certs, pen test results, and an initial security questionnaire answered.
[04:44] Maya: Absolutely. Liam, can you send the questionnaire now or list the top docs?
[04:51] Liam: I'll send a consolidated list after this call — SOC2 type II, ISO27001, pen test summary, architecture diagram, KMS integration details, and a contact for incident response.
[05:06] Maya: Great, we'll include that. Jenna, for procurement — is pricing approval gated by a particular committee?
[05:14] Jenna: Yes, pricing needs exec sign-off for anything over $150k ARR. For pilot and POC budgets we can often approve smaller pilots without exec if procurement signs off.
[05:27] Maya: Good, we'll size the pilot to be below the exec threshold then. Carlos, can we propose a pilot scope and cost?
[05:35] Carlos: Yep. I'm thinking a 4-week pilot: ingest 10k requests/day with a dedicated small pod, runway for stress tests and one benchmark day. Pricing we'll put in a spreadsheet — will show hosted and dedicated cost comparisons.
[05:54] Evan: For the benchmark, can you run it in our staging VPC? We want realistic networking and egress.
[06:03] Carlos: Yes, we can run benchmark in staging. We'll need a short network setup window and a service account. I'll coordinate with Asha for the runbook.
[06:17] Asha: I'll draft the onboarding checklist and include network steps, runbook, and contact matrix.
[06:25] Jenna: On SLAs, we need an uptime SLA + latency SLOs. We understand uptime is standard, but can you commit to a p99 latency SLO for our triage API?
[06:36] Maya: We offer uptime SLAs on Dedicated with credits for breaches. Latency SLOs for p99 are trickier because they depend on workload, but we can include target latency expectations and a remediation/rollback policy. For strict latency guarantees, Private on-prem sometimes is the best path.
[06:56] Liam: Would Redwood accept a clause for scheduled capacity windows and guaranteed MIPS for our tier?
[07:04] Maya: We can propose reserved capacity commitments for the Dedicated plan and outline run-rate commitments in the MSA. We'll send a suggested clause.
[07:14] Dr. Priya: One more security question — data encryption in transit and at rest? Also, do you tokenize or log responses that may contain PHI?
[07:25] Carlos: All traffic TLS 1.2+, at rest encryption with customer-managed keys available. We recommend disabling full response logging for PHI; instead, metadata-only logs or hashed outputs. We'll include configuration guidance.
[07:41] Jenna: Great. On the DPA, our legal wants a 30-day data deletion guarantee after termination. Is that feasible?
[07:51] Maya: We can commit to deletion timelines; typical enterprise language is 30-90 days depending on backups. We'll propose 30 days for PHI workloads and document the deletion process.
[08:03] Evan: Regarding cost, our CFO asked for a model to project monthly spend at different QPS. Could we get a sample cost model?
[08:12] Carlos: We'll include a per-token and per-instance cost model in the spreadsheet and run sample scenarios. Also suggestions for batching and caching to reduce unit costs.
[08:25] Jenna: About procurement, is Redwood okay with standard PO + net30?
[08:31] Maya: Yes, net30 is standard for enterprise. For onboarding we'll accept PO and then invoice.
[08:38] Liam: Any concerns about subcontractors or third-party hosting? We need to disclose where data is processed.
[08:47] Maya: We'll list subprocessors and cloud regions; for Private we can avoid third-party processing. We'll put that in the DPA.
[08:58] Dr. Priya: Ok, sounds like we have alignment. Quick check — timeline recap?
[09:06] Jenna: Procurement aims to approve pricing and issue PO by 6/22. Legal needs redline by next week. Security wants docs in 3 business days.
[09:16] Maya: Our commitments: redline + security pack by 6/15, performance config + benchmark plan by 6/16, onboarding checklist by 6/18. Anything else?
[09:26] Evan: Can we get a short one-page diagram of network flow for our infra team?
[09:31] Carlos: Yes, i'll include a network diagram and sample VPC peering steps.
[09:38] Asha: i'll also propose a pilot kickoff date tentatively 6/23 pending redline sign-off.
[09:44] Jenna: Sounds good.
[09:48] Maya: Alright us°last thing, any competitor concerns? Were you evaluating others?
[09:53] Jenna: We looked at Anthropic for the hosted side and OpenAI for a quick POC, and Infratech for an infra-first approach. Security favored Redwood's Dedicated + Private options.
[10:06] Maya: Thanks, that's helpful. We'll make sure our packet addresses the differentiators: consistent SLOs, audit logs, and clear KMS/HSM steps.
[10:16] Liam: One small point — incident response SLA, we need a 1-hour on-call response for Sev1s. Is that in scope?
[10:24] Maya: We can include a clause for 1-hour initial acknowledgment and a 4-hour incident mitigation target for enterprise SLA add-on. We'll surface it in the MSA options.
[10:36] Dr. Priya: Perfect. Anything else?
[10:40] Jenna: No, that's it from procurement. Thanks everyone.

[End of recorded transcript — auto-generated timestamps approximate; transcription imperfect in places.]
